app.title: BIXI Demand Forecasting and Rebalancing
app.question: How many departures and arrivals should we expect at each station, and where should bicycles be redistributed?
app.station_names_note: Station names are shown in their original form.

pages.planned_step: Planned for step {step} of the build.

overview.description: Headline numbers, forecast status, and key findings for the selected stations.

trip_analysis.description: Hourly, daily, and seasonal patterns of departures and arrivals.

station_map.description: Interactive map of stations with trip volume, net flow, and forecast overlays.

forecasts.description: Departure and arrival forecasts for the next 24 hours, with prediction intervals.

rebalancing.description: Scenario analysis of redistribution plans under explicit assumptions about starting bike inventory and station capacity.

model_performance.description: Baselines versus machine-learning models, time-based backtests, and error analysis.

methodology.description: Data sources, station selection, modelling choices, assumptions, and limitations.

methodology.assumption_1: Observed trips are not the same as true demand: when a station is empty or full, unmet demand is never recorded.
methodology.assumption_2: Periods outside the operating season are excluded from modelling.
methodology.assumption_3: Rebalancing results depend on assumed starting inventory and station capacity; they are scenario estimates, not measured outcomes.
methodology.assumption_4: 24-hour forecasts use only information available at prediction time (weather forecasts, not observed weather).

analysis.kpi_weekend_help: Average departures on a weekend day as a share of an average weekday.
analysis.profile_caption: Average departures and arrivals in each hour of the day, for the selected stations and days.
analysis.net_title: When do stations fill up or empty?
analysis.net_caption: Arrivals minus departures in each hour. Blue bars: the selection gains bikes. Red bars: it loses bikes.
analysis.heatmap_caption: Darker cells mean more departures. Compare the two commuting peaks on weekdays with the single afternoon peak on weekends.
analysis.trend_caption: Departures per day (7-day average), one line per year. The modelled season runs from April 15 to November 15.
analysis.alt_profile: Line chart of average departures and arrivals by hour of day
analysis.alt_net: Bar chart of average net bike change by hour of day
analysis.alt_heatmap: Heatmap of average departures by weekday and hour
analysis.alt_trend: Line chart of daily departures across the season for each year

map.legend: Blue circles gain bikes (more arrivals than departures); red circles lose bikes. Circle size shows total trips. Grey dots are the rest of the BIXI network. Values are averages per day for the selected years, day types, and time of day.
map.share_note: Share of docks is the average net change divided by the station's number of docks. Above 100%, the change is larger than the whole station, so it cannot be absorbed without moving bikes, whatever the starting inventory.
map.alt: Map of the 50 study stations, coloured by net bike change and sized by trip volume
